plan: 2 Samuel 2:1-7, 8-11, 12-17, 18–3:1; 2 Samuel 3:2-5; 1 Chronicles 3:1-4a; 2 Samuel 23:8-17; 1 Chronicles 11:10-19; 2 Samuel 23:18-39; 1 Chronicles 11:20-47

readings.title: Dawid Anointed Sovereign over Yehudah
readings.subtitle: Dawid Seeks YeHoVaH's Direction
readings.text: [2 Samuel 2:1] And it came to be after this that Dawid inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Do I go up to any of the cities of Yehudah?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Go up.”</dq> Dawid then said, “Where do I go up?” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“To Ḥeḇron.”</dq> [2] So Dawid went up there, and his two wives also, Aḥino‛am the Yizre‛ĕlitess, and Aḇigayil the widow of Naḇal the Karmelite. [3] And Dawid brought up <dn>את</dn> the men who were with him, every man with his household, and they dwelt in the cities of Ḥeḇron. [4] And the men of Yehudah came, and there they anointed <dn>את</dn> Dawid sovereign over the house of Yehudah. And they told Dawid, saying, “The men of Yaḇĕsh Gil‛aḏ were the ones who buried Sha’ul.” [5] Dawid then sent messengers to the men of Yaḇĕsh Gil‛aḏ, and said to them, “Blessed are you of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that you have shown <dn>את</dn> this loving-commitment to your master, to Sha’ul, and buried <dn>את</dn> him. [6] “And now, let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> show loving-commitment and truth to you. And I also show you <dn>את</dn> this good, because you have done this deed. [7] “And now, let your hands be strong, and be brave, for your master Sha’ul is dead, and also the house of Yehudah have anointed <dn>את</dn> me sovereign over them.”

readings.title: Ishbosheth Anointed over Yisra'el
readings.subtitle: A Divided Kingdom
readings.text: [2 Samuel 2:8] But Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, commander of Sha’ul’s army, took <dn>את</dn> Ishbosheth the son of Sha’ul and brought him over to Maḥanayim, [9] and made him sovereign over Gil‛aḏ, and over the Ashurites, and over Yizre‛ĕl, and over Ephrayim, and over Binyamin, and over all Yisra’ĕl. [10] Ishbosheth, Sha’ul’s son, was forty years old when he began to reign over Yisra’ĕl, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Yehudah followed Dawid. [11] And the time that Dawid was sovereign in Ḥeḇron over the house of Yehudah was seven years and six months.

readings.title: The Clash at Gib'on
readings.subtitle: The Conflict Escalates
readings.text: [2 Samuel 2:12] And Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, and the servants of Ishbosheth the son of Sha’ul, went out from Maḥanayim to Giḇ‛on. [13] And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah, and the servants of Dawid, went out and met them by the pool of Giḇ‛on. And they sat down, one on one side of the pool and the other on the other side of the pool. [14] And Aḇnĕr said to Yo’aḇ, “Please let the young men arise and play before us.” And Yo’aḇ said, “Let them arise.” [15] Then they arose and went over by number, twelve from Binyamin, even of Ishbosheth the son of Sha’ul, and twelve from the servants of Dawid. [16] And each one caught his opponent by the head and thrust his sword in his opponent’s side, so they fell down together. And that place was called Ḥelqath Hatstsurim, which is in Giḇ‛on. [17] And the battle was very fierce that day, and Aḇnĕr and the men of Yisra’ĕl were beaten before the servants of Dawid.

readings.title: The Pursuit of Abner
readings.subtitle: The Fall of Asahel
readings.text: [2 Samuel 2:18] And the three sons of Tseruyah were there: Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai and Asahĕl. And Asahĕl was as fleet of foot as a gazelle which is in the field. [19] And Asahĕl pursued Aḇnĕr, and in going he did not turn to the right or to the left from following Aḇnĕr. [20] And Aḇnĕr looked behind him and said, “Are you Asahĕl?” And he answered, “I am.” [21] And Aḇnĕr said to him, “Turn aside to your right hand or to your left, and lay hold on one of the young men and take <dn>את</dn> his armour for yourself.” But Asahĕl would not turn aside from following him. [22] And Aḇnĕr said again to Asahĕl, “Turn aside from following me. Why should I smite you to the ground? How then could I lift up my face to Yo’aḇ your brother?” [23] But he refused to turn aside. Therefore Aḇnĕr smote him in the stomach with the blunt end of the spear, so that the spear came out of his back. And he fell down there and died on the spot. And it came to be that as many as came to the place where Asahĕl fell down and died, stood still. [24] But Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai pursued Aḇnĕr. And the sun was going down when they came to the hill of Ammah, which is before Giyah by the way to the wilderness of Giḇ‛on. [25] And the children of Binyamin gathered together behind Aḇnĕr and became one troop, and stood on the top of a hill. [26] And Aḇnĕr called to Yo’aḇ and said, “Should the sword devour forever? Do you not know that it shall be bitter in the latter end? And how long will it be until you command the people to turn back from pursuing their brothers?” [27] And Yo’aḇ said, “As <dn>Elohim</dn> lives, unless you had spoken, surely then by morning all the people would have given up pursuing their brothers.” [28] And Yo’aḇ blew a ram’s horn, and all the people stood still and did not pursue Yisra’ĕl any longer, nor did they fight any more. [29] And Aḇnĕr and his men went through the Araḇah all that night, and crossed <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn, and went through all Bithron, and came to Maḥanayim. [30] And Yo’aḇ returned from pursuing Aḇnĕr. And when he had gathered <dn>את</dn> all the people together, there were missing of Dawid’s servants nineteen men and Asahĕl. [31] But the servants of Dawid had smitten of Binyamin and of Aḇnĕr’s men, three hundred and sixty men who died. [32] And they took up <dn>את</dn> Asahĕl and buried him in his father’s burial-site, which was in Bĕyth Leḥem. And Yo’aḇ and his men went all night, and they came to Ḥeḇron at daybreak. [2 Samuel 3:1] And there was a long war between the house of Sha’ul and the house of Dawid. But Dawid grew stronger and stronger, and the house of Sha’ul grew weaker and weaker.

readings.title: The Sons of Dawid
readings.subtitle: The Family Established in Hebron
readings.text: [2 Samuel 3:2] And sons were born to Dawid in Ḥeḇron: His first-born was Amnon by Aḥino‛am the Yizre‛ĕlitess; [3] and his second, Kilaḇ, by Aḇigayil the widow of Naḇal the Karmelite; and the third, Aḇshalom the son of Ma‛aḵah, the daughter of Talmai, sovereign of Geshur; [4] and the fourth, Aḏoniyah the son of Ḥaggith; and the fifth, Shephatyah the son of Aḇital; [5] and the sixth, Yithre‛am, by Dawid’s wife Eglah. These were born to Dawid in Ḥeḇron. [1 Chronicles 3:1] And these were the sons of Dawid who were born to him in Ḥeḇron: The first-born was Amnon, by Aḥino‛am the Yizre‛ĕlitess; the second, Dani’ĕl, by Aḇigayil the Karmelitess; [2] the third, Aḇshalom the son of Ma‛aḵah, the daughter of Talmai, sovereign of Geshur; the fourth, Aḏoniyahu the son of Ḥaggith; [3] the fifth, Shephatyah, by Aḇital; the sixth, Yithre‛am, by his wife Eglah. [4] Six were born to him in Ḥeḇron.

readings.title: Dawid's Three Mighty Men
readings.subtitle: Water from the Well of Beyth Lehem
readings.text: [2 Samuel 23:8] These are the names of the mighty men whom Dawid had: Yoshĕḇ-Bashsheḇeth the Taḥkemonite, chief among the captains. He was called Adinah the Etsnite, because he had killed eight hundred men at one time. [9] And after him was El‛azar son of Doḏo, the Aḥoḥite, one of the three mighty men with Dawid when they reproached the Pelishtites who were gathered there for battle, and the men of Yisra’ĕl had retreated. [10] He arose and smote the Pelishtites until his hand was weary, and his hand clung to the sword. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> wrought a great deliverance that day. And the people returned after him only to strip the slain. [11] And after him was Shammah son of Agĕ, the Hararite. And the Pelishtites gathered into a troop where there was a piece of ground full of lentils, and the people fled from the Pelishtites. [12] But he took his stand in the middle of the field, and delivered it, and smote <dn>את</dn> the Pelishtites. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> wrought a great deliverance. [13] And three of the thirty chief men went down at harvest time and came to Dawid at the cave of Aḏullam, while the troop of Pelishtites encamped in the Valley of Repha’im. [14] And Dawid was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Pelishtites was then in Bĕyth Leḥem. [15] And Dawid had a strong desire and said, “Oh, that someone would give me a drink of the water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem, which is by the gate!” [16] And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Pelishtites, and drew water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem that was by the gate, and took it and brought it to Dawid. But he would not drink it, and poured <dn>את</dn> it out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [17] And he said, “Far be it from me, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that I should do this! Is it the blood of the men who went in jeopardy of their lives?” And he would not drink it. This the three mighty men did. [1 Chronicles 11:10] And these were the heads of the mighty men whom Dawid had, who strengthened themselves with him in his reign, with all Yisra’ĕl, to make him sovereign, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning Yisra’ĕl. [11] And this is the number of the mighty men whom Dawid had: Yashaḇ‛am the son of a Ḥaḵmonite, chief of the captains; he lifted up <dn>את</dn> his spear against three hundred, slain at one time. [12] And after him was El‛azar son of Doḏo, the Aḥoḥite, who was one of the three mighty men. [13] He was with Dawid at Pas Dammim. Now there the Pelishtites were gathered for battle, and there was a piece of ground full of barley. And the people fled from the Pelishtites, [14] but they took their stand in the midst of that field, and delivered it, and smote <dn>את</dn> the Pelishtites. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved them by a great deliverance. [15] And three of the thirty chief men went down to the rock to Dawid, into the cave of Aḏullam, and the army of the Pelishtites encamped in the Valley of Repha’im. [16] And Dawid was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Pelishtites was then in Bĕyth Leḥem. [17] And Dawid had a strong desire and said, “Oh, that someone would give me a drink of water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem, which is by the gate!” [18] And the three broke through the camp of the Pelishtites, and drew water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem that was by the gate, and took it and brought it to Dawid. But Dawid would not drink it, but poured <dn>את</dn> it out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [19] And he said, “Far be it from me, O my <dn>Elohim</dn>, that I should do this! Should I drink the blood of these men who went in jeopardy of their lives? For at the risk of their lives they brought it.” So he would not drink it. This the three mighty men did.

readings.title: Dawid's Thirty Mighty Men
readings.subtitle: The Records of Samuel
readings.text: [2 Samuel 23:18] And Aḇishai the brother of Yo’aḇ, the son of Tseruyah, was chief of another three. And he lifted up <dn>את</dn> his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name among these three. [19] Was he not the most esteemed of three? Therefore he became their commander, but he did not come up to the first three. [20] And Benayah son of Yehoyaḏa, the son of a brave man from Qaḇtse’ĕl, great in deeds, smote <dn>את</dn> two lion-like heroes of Mo’aḇ. He also went down and smote <dn>את</dn> a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day. [21] And he smote <dn>את</dn> an Mitsrite, a spectacular man. And the Mitsrite had a spear in his hand, but he went down to him with a staff, and snatched <dn>את</dn> the spear out of the Mitsrite’s hand, and killed him with his own spear. [22] This Benayah son of Yehoyaḏa did, and won a name among three mighty men. [23] He was more esteemed than the thirty, but he did not come up to the first three. And Dawid appointed him over his guard. [24] Asahĕl the brother of Yo’aḇ was one of the thirty; Elḥanan son of Doḏo of Bĕyth Leḥem; [25] Shammah the Ḥaroḏite, Eliqa the Ḥaroḏite; [26] Ḥelets the Palti, Ira son of Iqqĕsh the Teqoyite; [27] Aḇi‛ezer the Anathothite, Meḇunnai the Ḥushathite; [28] Tsalmon the Aḥoḥite, Maharai the Netophathite; [29] Ḥĕleḇ son of Ba‛anah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Riḇai from Giḇ‛ah of the children of Binyamin; [30] Benayahu a Pir‛athonite, Hiddai from the wadis of Ga‛ash; [31] Aḇi-Alḇon the Arḇathite, Azmaweth the Barḥumite; [32] Elyaḥba the Sha‛alḇonite, of the sons of Yashen: Yehonathan; [33] Shammah the Hararite, Aḥiam son of Sharar the Hararite; [34] Eliphelet son of Aḥasbai, the son of a Ma‛aḵathite, Eli‛am son of Aḥithophel the Gilonite; [35] Ḥetsrai the Karmelite, Pa‛arai the Arḇite; [36] Yig’al son of Nathan of Tsoḇah, Bani the Gaḏite; [37] Tseleq the Ammonite, Naḥarai the Be’ĕrothite, armour-bearer of Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah; [38] Ira the Yithrite, Garĕḇ the Yithrite; [39] Uriyah the Ḥittite: thirty-seven in all.

readings.title: Dawid's Thirty Mighty Men
readings.subtitle: The Records of the Chronicles
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 11:20] And Aḇshai the brother of Yo’aḇ, he was chief of another three. And he lifted up <dn>את</dn> his spear against three hundred, slain, and won a name among these three. [21] Of the three he was more esteemed than the other two, and he became their commander, but he did not come up to the first three. [22] Benayah son of Yehoyaḏa, the son of a brave man from Qaḇtse’ĕl, great in deeds, smote <dn>את</dn> two lion-like heroes of Mo’aḇ. He also went down and smote <dn>את</dn> a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day. [23] And he smote <dn>את</dn> an Mitsrite, a man of great height, five cubits tall. In the Mitsrite’s hand there was a spear like a weaver’s beam, and he went down to him with a staff, and snatched <dn>את</dn> the spear out of the Mitsrite’s hand, and killed him with his own spear. [24] This Benayah son of Yehoyaḏa did, and won a name among the three mighty men. [25] See, he was more esteemed than the thirty, but he did not come up to the first three. And Dawid appointed him over his guard. [26] And the mighty men of the armies were Asahĕl the brother of Yo’aḇ, Elḥanan son of Doḏo of Bĕyth Leḥem, [27] Shammoth the Harorite, Ḥelets the Pelonite, [28] Ira son of Iqqĕsh the Teqoyite, Aḇi‛ezer the Anathothite, [29] Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite, Ilai the Aḥoḥite, [30] Maharai the Netophathite, Ḥĕleḏ son of Ba‛anah the Netophathite, [31] Ithai son of Riḇai of Giḇ‛ah, of the children of Binyamin, Benayah the Pir‛athonite, [32] Ḥurai of the wadis of Ga‛ash, Aḇi’ĕl the Arḇathite, [33] Azmaweth the Baḥarumite, Elyaḥba the Sha‛alḇonite, [34] the sons of Hashĕm the Gizonite, Yehonathan son of Shagĕ the Hararite, [35] Aḥiam son of Saḵar the Hararite, Eliphal the son of Ur, [36] Ḥĕpher the Mĕḵĕrathite, Aḥiyah the Pelonite, [37] Ḥetsro the Karmelite, Na‛arai the son of Ezbai, [38] Yo’ĕl the brother of Nathan, Miḇḥar the son of Hagri, [39] Tseleq the Ammonite, Naḥarai the Bĕrothite, the armour-bearer of Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah, [40] Ira the Yithrite, Garĕḇ the Yithrite, [41] Uriyah the Ḥittite, Zaḇaḏ son of Aḥlai, [42] Aḏina son of Shiza the Re’uḇĕnite, a head of the Re’uḇĕnites, and thirty with him, [43] Ḥanan son of Ma‛aḵah, and Yoshaphat the Mithnite, [44] Uzziya the Ashterathite, Shama and Ye‛i’ĕl the sons of Ḥotham the Aro‛ĕrite, [45] Yeḏi‛a’ĕl son of Shimri, and Yoḥa his brother, the Titsite, [46] Eli’ĕl the Maḥawite, and Yeriḇai, and Yoshawyah, the sons of Elna‛am, and Yithmah the Mo’aḇite, [47] Eli’ĕl, and Oḇĕḏ, and Ya‛asi’ĕl the Metsoḇayite.
